steps: Intellectual property rights protect the creations and work of authors, artists, inventors and software developers.
Respecting these rights gives creators proper credit and control over how their work is used.
It encourages creativity and prevents the unauthorised copying or use of someone else's work.
items.finalAnswer: Respecting intellectual property rights protects creators and encourages creativity.

steps: Software piracy is the illegal copying, sharing, downloading or use of software without the owner's permission or a valid licence.
It deprives developers and companies of payment for their work.
Pirated software may contain viruses or other harmful programs and may not receive updates or support.
items.finalAnswer: Software piracy is unauthorised software use that harms creators and can put devices at risk.

steps: Check who wrote the information and whether the author or organisation is qualified and trustworthy.
Check the publication date to make sure the information is current.
Prefer reliable sources such as educational institutions, recognised organisations and reputable publications.
Compare the information with other trustworthy sources and check whether evidence and references are provided.
Consider whether the source is biased or trying to persuade or sell something.
items.finalAnswer: Check the source's author, date, reputation, evidence and agreement with other reliable sources.

steps: Do not share personal information, such as your address, phone number or passwords, on websites while researching online.
items.finalAnswer: Keep personal information private while researching online.

steps: Spending more time on the internet than intended or being unable to reduce the time spent online.
Neglecting schoolwork, sleep, hobbies or responsibilities because of internet use.
Feeling restless, upset or anxious when unable to use the internet.
Continuing to use the internet despite problems it causes in daily life or relationships.
items.finalAnswer: Excessive use, neglected responsibilities and distress when offline may be signs of internet addiction.

steps: Responsible computer usage means using computers and digital resources safely, ethically and appropriately.
It helps protect users, devices and information, and encourages respectful and lawful behaviour online.
Choose hardware that meets the user's needs and is reliable; suitable hardware can improve safety and efficiency.
Choose genuine, appropriate software from trusted sources and keep it updated to reduce security risks and support efficient work.
Check that the software is compatible with the computer's hardware and operating system so that devices and programs work together correctly.
items.finalAnswer: Responsible computer use protects users and information; suitable, trusted and compatible hardware and software improve safety and efficiency.

steps: Read and follow the safety instructions for each device and digital platform.
Use strong, unique passwords and do not share them; enable extra authentication when available.
Install software and updates from trusted sources, and use suitable security software.
Do not open suspicious links, attachments or downloads, and do not share sensitive information on untrusted sites.
Use devices carefully, keep them secure, and log out of accounts when using a shared device.
Back up important data regularly and report suspicious activity or security problems to a trusted adult or the appropriate authority.
items.finalAnswer: Follow security guidance, use strong passwords and updates, avoid suspicious content, protect data and report problems.

steps: Data ethics is the responsible and fair collection, use, storage and sharing of data.
Transparency means clearly explaining what data is collected, why it is collected and how it will be used.
Respect for privacy means protecting personal and sensitive information and using it only with proper permission and for an appropriate purpose.
Accountability means accepting responsibility for the handling of data and taking action if it is misused, exposed or inaccurate.
These principles build trust, protect people's rights and help prevent harm caused by misuse of information.
items.finalAnswer: Data ethics means handling information responsibly through transparency, respect for privacy and accountability.
